en.name: 10mm Auto Xtreme Penetrator
en.description: The 10mm Auto (10x25mm) was developed in the early 1980s around Jeff Cooper's idea of a flat-shooting, hard-hitting service pistol cartridge, and at full power it is one of the strongest rounds a standard-size pistol can fire. Underwood's load with the 140-grain Lehigh Defense Xtreme Penetrator in a nickel-plated case: a lead-free, solid copper bullet whose cross-shaped nose does not expand. The four scoops throw fluid sideways and the bullet keeps all of its weight, driving deep through barriers and soft armor.
